## Overview

ConnectX brings IP telephony, self-service, routing and agent operations into one contact-center platform. An AI voice agent handles supported questions using approved content and connected systems, with identity checks and a contextual handoff when a person is needed. Agents work across voice, chat, email, WhatsApp and social channels, while supervisors review recordings, quality scores, queues and workforce performance. Customer-managed deployment supports existing IP handsets and integration with banking, CRM and operational systems.

The AI agent sits in the core of the platform rather than in front of it. It answers only from approved content and connected systems, applies an identity policy your risk team reads and edits as a table, and hands the conversation to a skilled agent with full context when a request is sensitive or unsupported. Language coverage, supported operations, deployment topology and retention are confirmed during evaluation.

## Problems we solve

- **A contact center assembled from separate products.** Telephony, IVR, routing, agent desktop, supervisor tooling, recording, omnichannel, reporting and workforce management in one platform, one admin console and one database.
- **Callers queue for questions a system could answer.** The AI agent answers supported questions from approved sources and connected systems, and only the rest reach a person.
- **Customers repeat themselves on every channel.** One universal queue and one customer history across voice, chat, email, WhatsApp and social.
- **Every prompt or routing change waits on a developer.** Prompts, menu words, wrap-up codes and routing rules are maintained by your own business team in the console.

## AI inside

AI supports voice conversations, knowledge-based answers, transcription, quality scoring and workforce forecasting. Identity policies and approved sources govern responses; sensitive operations are handed to a human. Connect your own Claude or Gemini API key in Settings and pay your provider directly.

- Voice and chat conversation in Bangla and English

## Inside ConnectX: the product tour

1. **Agent workspace.** An illustrative call arrives with verified identity and context from the AI handoff.
2. **Routing and callbacks.** Review skill queues and callbacks before assigning the next available agent.
3. **Quality review.** Review a recording and transcript before accepting AI-assisted coaching suggestions.
4. **Identity and policy.** Review the identity tier a request needs before any information is disclosed.
5. **Service level and wallboard.** Watch queues against targets, then open the conversation behind a breach.
6. **Omnichannel queue.** Watch one queue hold every channel, with the customer's history attached.
7. **Value board.** Read how many conversations finished without a person, and why the rest did not.

## How it works: your first week

1. **Confirm scope and workspace.** Agree channel coverage, concurrent-agent count, supported operations and the implementation plan with the delivery team.
2. **Connect trunks and systems.** Connect your authorized SIP trunk provider and the business systems the agent reads from, then verify a test call end to end.
3. **Define the identity policy.** Write the identity tiers and the factors each operation requires in a table your risk team reads and edits.
4. **Prepare approved content.** Load the greetings, answers and knowledge articles the agent may use, in each language you support.
5. **Design menus and routing.** Set the menu words, skills, priorities, the VIP list and the wrap-up codes in the console, and test each path before go-live.
6. **Review and improve.** Read the value board, the service levels and the handover reasons, then adjust prompts, menus and rules from what you see.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is ConnectX a standalone product?**

Yes. Telephony, IVR, routing, agent desktop, supervisor tooling, recording, omnichannel, reporting, workforce management and outbound dialing ship as one platform, with one admin console and one database. A separate telephony, recording or workforce product is not required.

**What does the AI agent actually do?**

It answers supported voice and chat questions using approved content and connected systems, applies your identity policy before disclosing anything, and hands the conversation to an agent with full context when a request is sensitive or unsupported.

**Which languages does it handle?**

The agent is built for Bangla and English, and for the two mixed in the same conversation, locked to the language the customer chose rather than guessed. Confirm the coverage your customers need during evaluation.

**Can customers complete transactions without an agent?**

Supported self-service operations are connected to your authorized systems and governed by your identity policy. Which operations are enabled, and at which identity tier, is defined by your own risk team during evaluation.

**How do we change a prompt or a routing rule?**

In the admin console. Prompts, menu words, wrap-up codes, the VIP list and routing rules are maintained by your business team, with no code change and no release.

**What do agents need on their desk?**

Agents answer and end calls in the browser, with nothing to install on the desktop. A SIP softphone and desk handsets are scoped in the implementation plan, and which handset and headset models are supported is confirmed during evaluation.

**Where does ConnectX run, and what should we review?**

ConnectX is a customer-managed deployment on infrastructure you control. Review telephony and trunk requirements, identity policies, integration specifications, retention, training and support terms during evaluation. No hosting region or certification is implied.

**What is in the first release, and what comes later?**

The AI agent, IVR self-service, ACD and skill routing, the agent desktop, the supervisor console, the knowledge base, the wallboard and the value board are delivered first, with SNMP traps and Syslog for your monitoring team. Call recording and quality scoring, workforce management and the outbound dialer, the drag-and-drop flow designer, call transfer and conference, and the Power BI and CRM connections are scoped in the implementation plan and delivered with the Enterprise tier. The split is agreed in writing during evaluation.
